events.title: Economics may decide outcome of Iran-US standoff
events.summary: The next phase of the Iran–US standoff may be decided not on the battlefield, but by how much economic pressure each side can withstand.

events.title: Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf seek Araghchi’s ouster over 'subservience' to Guards
events.summary: Iran's president and parliament speaker are seeking Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s removal, accusing him of following the Revolutionary Guard chief’s instructions in nuclear talks without informing the president, two sources familiar with the matter told Iran International.

events.title: US forms new coalition to secure Hormuz, asks partners to join
events.summary: The United States has asked partner countries to join its newly formed Maritime Freedom Coalition to help secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf waterways, according to a State Department cable.

events.title: Iranians denounce tiered internet plan as discriminatory and corrupt
events.summary: Iranians condemned selective access to restricted internet services as discriminatory and corrupt in messages to Iran International, urging others to reject the scheme in recent days.

events.title: How the Taliban tilted toward Iran during wartime tensions
events.summary: Taliban leaders and affiliated figures voiced support for Iran after Israeli strikes in June 2025 and later US threats, signaling a limited and conditional alignment despite longstanding disputes with Tehran.

events.title: Iran ranks near bottom as press curbs deepen worldwide
events.summary: Iran ranked among the world’s worst countries for press freedom in 2026 as global conditions hit a 25-year low, with legal pressure on journalists intensifying across multiple regions, Reporters Without Borders said.

events.title: Soaring prices push medicine beyond Iranians' reach
events.summary: Medicine prices in Iran have surged sharply in recent weeks, with some drugs rising by as much as 380%, according to reports received by Iran International, as the country grapples with soaring inflation, a collapsing currency and worsening wartime disruption.

events.title: As Tehran praises Moscow, critics ask where Russia was
events.summary: As Iranian officials continue to tout a “strategic partnership” with Russia, rare public criticism has emerged over Moscow’s muted response to the recent war.

events.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with German Foreign Minister Wadephul

The Secretary and Foreign Minister discussed the security situation in the region and underscored the importance of securing freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Iran football chief with IRGC ties sent back by Canada after arrival
events.summary: Iran's football chief Mehdi Taj, once a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was sent back from Canada just hours after landing, according to a government source who spoke to Iran International.

events.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Cooper
events.summary: Office of the Spokesperson Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Cooper Readout April 29, 2026 The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper on the occasion of King Charles III and Queen Camilla’s visit to the United States.  The Secretary and Foreign Secretary discussed the urgent need to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Even state media sounds alarm as Iran’s economy sinks
events.summary: Iran’s worsening economic crisis is drawing unusually blunt warnings from state media and establishment voices as war, inflation and shortages squeeze households and expose the limits of the government’s response.

events.title: Iran currency plunges as dollar crosses 1.8 million in open market
events.summary: The US dollar passed 1.81 million rials on Iran’s open market on Wednesday, rising nearly 8% in a single day as the country’s economic crisis worsened under the strain of maritime blockade, stalled diplomacy and mounting pressure on households.

events.title: Tehran is pricing out its daughters
events.summary: For years, young women from smaller cities and conservative families came to Tehran to study, to work, to breathe. Now, one by one, many are being forced to leave.

events.title: Iran war clouds summer travel as jet fuel costs soar
events.summary: European airlines are facing their biggest test since the COVID-19 pandemic as the Iran war drives up jet fuel prices, disrupts Middle East routes and raises concerns about possible fuel shortages ahead of the summer holiday season.

events.title: Iran taps reserves again as inflation bites and layoffs mount
events.summary: Iran has once again tapped its sovereign wealth reserves to fund essential imports, highlighting the growing strain on an economy battered by war, inflation and a rapidly weakening currency.

events.summary: A widening split over how to deal with the United States has reached the deepest layers of Iran’s hardline establishment, surfacing in state-linked media and among factions that have long presented a united front under the banner of revolutionary loyalty.

events.title: Calls for secrecy in Tehran reflect divisions over US talks
events.summary: As efforts continue to revive talks with the United States, Iranian lawmakers and state-linked outlets are increasingly calling for secrecy around negotiations.

events.title: Three layers of mistrust behind US-Iran deadlock
events.summary: Deep-rooted mistrust continues to stand in the way of any meaningful thaw between Iran and the United States despite renewed diplomacy after weeks of war.

events.title: Iran’s water crisis: Mafia or destruction by design?
events.summary: Iran’s water crisis did not begin with a “water mafia,” but with a state model built on self-sufficiency, laws that gave the government broad control over water, subsidized water, and mega-projects that turned scarcity into a map of conflict.

events.title: Two months offline: Iran blackout drives losses, access splits
events.summary: Iran’s near-total shutdown of the global internet reached 60 days on Tuesday, worsening economic losses and social restrictions as authorities move toward selective access for some users and businesses.

events.title: Iran’s foreign trade suffers wartime collapse
events.summary: Iran’s foreign trade has suffered a sharp contraction in the first month of war with the United States and Israel, newly released customs data show, signaling a severe blow to the country’s already fragile economy.

events.title: Did Araghchi’s tour signal leverage or isolation?
events.summary: In Tehran, Abbas Araghchi’s whirlwind regional tour is being presented as evidence that Iran still has diplomatic options and regional leverage.

events.title: Why a blockade would not halt Iran’s oil overnight
events.summary: Amid Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the ensuing US blockade, an old energy fantasy has resurfaced that cutting off a country’s oil exports works like flipping a switch. But reality is less cinematic and far more uncomfortable.

events.title: Iran, US clash at UN over Strait of Hormuz closure
events.summary: Iran and the United States traded accusations at the United Nations on Monday over the Strait of Hormuz, as the archfoes’ weeks-long standoff over the strategic waterway continued to disrupt global energy supplies and world trade.

events.title: Iran football chief with IRGC past to visit Canada for FIFA event
events.summary: A Revolutionary Guards commander turned Iran's football chief has been granted special permission to enter Canada for a FIFA event despite being otherwise inadmissible, according to government sources who spoke to Iran International.

events.title: Iran's top security council holds meeting over fears of renewed protests
events.summary: Iran’s Supreme National Security Council has held a meeting to address growing concerns among security agencies over a possible resurgence of protests, sources familiar with the discussions told Iran International.

events.title: New intelligence exposes IRGC-linked network targeting Israeli, Western sites
events.summary: New intelligence obtained by Iran International reveals the identities of operatives in an IRGC-linked espionage and assassination network, including a foreign cleric trained in Qom who allegedly coordinated attacks targeting Israeli and Western interests.

events.title: Iran designers reject ‘discriminatory’ tiered internet access
events.summary: Iran’s Graphic Designers Society refused to make a collective request for the so-called “Internet Pro” access for its members, calling the tiered internet plan “discriminatory.”

events.title: Is Ghalibaf becoming Iran’s Khrushchev?
events.summary: Reports that Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf may have been sidelined from Iran’s negotiations with the United States have revived an old question from Soviet history: can an insider reform a rigid ideological system without becoming one of its casualties?

events.title: Iran’s new military-led order may mean greater dangers abroad
events.summary: The Islamic Republic that has emerged from the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei may prove more operationally aggressive than the one it replaces, analysts say.

events.title: Is the US blockade working? It depends who you ask
events.summary: Recent tracking data suggesting Iran is still moving millions of barrels of crude despite a US naval blockade has raised fresh questions about the effectiveness of Washington’s effort to choke off Tehran’s oil exports.

events.title: The hidden target in US war on Iran may be China
events.summary: As Washington and Tehran navigate a fragile ceasefire, one of the biggest questions looming over the conflict may not be about Iran at all—but China.

events.title: Unity or fracture? Tehran battles Trump’s narrative of disarray
events.summary: Assertions by US President Donald Trump that Iran’s leadership is divided, and Tehran’s increasingly coordinated effort to deny it, have thrust the issue of unity to the center of the standoff between the two countries.

events.title: Iran nurses reject special internet access amid blackout
events.summary: Iran’s nursing organization said on Sunday it would not seek special internet access for its members until restrictions on international internet access were lifted for the public.

events.title: UK releases man jailed for spying on Iran International in 2023 terror plot
events.summary: A man jailed in the UK for conducting surveillance on Iran International has been released early and deported to Austria, despite being sentenced to three-and-a-half years in prison for gathering intelligence that could have aided a terrorist attack.

events.title: US should use Iran talks leverage to help Iranian people, veteran journalist says
events.summary: With US-Iran talks in Pakistan in doubt after Iran's foreign minister left Islamabad and President Trump canceled the planned trip by US negotiators, veteran journalist Eli Lake says Washington should use its leverage not only on the nuclear file, but to help the people of Iran.

events.title: Three Baha’i women jailed in southeast Iran, one of them pregnant
events.summary: Three Baha’i women from Rafsanjan, a city in Iran’s southeastern Kerman province, were sent to prison on Saturday to serve four-month sentences on the charge of “propaganda against the system,” according to information received by Iran International.

events.title: Iran executes protester over January uprising
events.summary: Iran executed a man on Saturday over his involvement in January anti-establishment protests, whom authorities said acted on behalf of Israel’s Mossad intelligence service.

events.title: Iranian national charged in US over migrant smuggling scheme
events.summary: A US federal indictment has charged an Iranian national with coordinating a large-scale migrant smuggling operation into the United States, the Justice Department said on Friday.

events.title: Iran’s economy after the March war: how bad can it get?
events.summary: Iran’s economy is heading into a period of sharp deterioration following the March war, with mounting pressure from inflation, currency depreciation and damage to key industries raising the risk of a broader crisis.

events.title: Starmer pledges to move on banning Iran's IRGC in next parliament session
events.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged to introduce legislation to proscribe Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in the next parliamentary session, in an interview with the Jewish Chronicle.

events.title: Behind Tehran’s unity show: The secret letter to the shadow king
events.summary: The real story behind Tehran’s sudden “unity” campaign did not begin with Donald Trump’s accusations of disarray within Iran’s leadership. It began with a secret letter to Mojtaba Khamenei.

events.title: UK’s LBC finds alleged Iran-linked channel hiring Britons for sabotage
events.summary: A journalist from LBC was offered payment by an alleged Iran-linked contact to carry out a street-level act of vandalism within hours of contact, the British broadcaster reported on Friday.

events.title: Iran officials project unity after Trump leadership remarks
events.summary: Iranian officials rushed to present a unified front after US President Donald Trump questioned who leads the Islamic Republic, highlighting sensitivities over internal divisions and uncertainty at the top of the political system.

events.title: Two men accused of spying for Iran to appear in London’s Old Bailey court
events.summary: Two men accused of carrying out surveillance on Jewish and Israeli-linked sites in London on behalf of Iran are due to appear at the Central Criminal Court on Friday for a preliminary hearing.

events.title: Iran to add US-Israel war to school curriculum amid ceasefire
events.summary: Iran plans to include the recent war with the United States and Israel in school textbooks, the education minister said, referring to what officials call the “third imposed war,” the latest conflict now under a ceasefire extended by US President Donald Trump.

events.title: Rapid deterioration of Iran-UAE ties threatens a critical trade lifeline
events.summary: Iran-UAE ties have unraveled over the past two months, beginning with Iranian airstrikes on Emirati targets during the US-led war and escalating into a crisis that now threatens one of Tehran’s most vital trade and financial channels.

events.title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
events.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing the names of one or more persons and aircraft that have been placed on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) based on OFAC's determination that one or more applicable legal criteria were satisfied. All property and interests in property subject to U.S. jurisdiction of these persons are blocked, and U.S. persons are generally prohibited from engaging in transactions with them. The aircraft placed on the SDN List have been identified as property in which a blocked person has an interest.

events.title: Tehran stocks head for reopening, but it risks triggering a new crisis
events.summary: After nearly two months of closure, Tehran’s stock market is preparing a phased reopening, but deep structural flaws, lack of transparency and uncertainty over US negotiations threaten to turn the restart into a fresh crisis.

events.title: Power vacuum in Tehran emboldens hardliners
events.summary: As debate over a ceasefire and renewed talks with the United States intensifies, the absence of a clear supreme arbiter in Tehran appears to be giving Iran’s hardliners more room to shape the narrative and to hinder any eventual agreement.

events.title: Disputes within Iran leadership blocked negotiators’ trip to Islamabad
events.summary: Divisions within Iran’s leadership prevented a negotiating team from traveling to Islamabad for talks with the US, Iran International has learned.

events.title: Inflation spikes, basic goods slip out of reach for Iranians, citizens say
events.summary: Food prices surged and basic goods slipped out of reach across Iran, citizens told Iran International in recent days, describing shortages and daily price jumps following a ceasefire that has coincided with worsening economic conditions.

events.title: Iran turns to citizenship and assets as tools of pressure beyond its borders
events.summary: The Islamic Republic is escalating its campaign against the diaspora, moving beyond domestic seizures to explore the confiscation of assets held by Iranians in foreign countries and possible revocation of their citizenship.

events.title: Exiled prince dismisses Iran negotiators as part of repression system
events.summary: The Islamic Republic’s negotiators in talks with the US are “different faces of the same machine,” that suppresses the Iranian people, exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi said at a press conference in Berlin on Thursday.

events.title: Who backs war now? Tehran flips the script
events.summary: Iran’s state broadcaster has sparked ridicule after claiming that 87% of Iranians support continuing the war with the United States, in a curious turn from early in the conflict where pro-war sentiments of an alienated populace was branded treachery.

The meeting underlined the determination of the international community to support freedom of navigation, to stand up for international law, and to protect global economic stability and energy security.

events.title: As Tehran digs in, ordinary Iranians pay the price
events.summary: As uncertainty clouds the next round of Iran-US talks, the economic pain of the war is mounting inside Iran and beyond, increasing pressure on both sides to find a way out.

events.title: Internet Pro or Censor Pro? Iran rolls out a new service
events.summary: Iran’s new “Internet Pro” rollout may tighten state control in the short term, but experts who spoke to Iran International question whether the Islamic Republic can sustain a class-based internet in one of the Middle East’s most connected societies.

events.title: Iran Guards say two ships seized in Hormuz after ceasefire extension
events.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said it had seized two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and directed them toward Iranian shores, hours after Donald Trump said the United States would extend a ceasefire with Iran.

events.title: IRGC-linked media hints at threat to Persian Gulf undersea internet cables
events.summary: IRGC-linked Tasnim has pointedly mapped the Persian Gulf’s undersea internet cables and cloud infrastructure in what appears to be a thinly veiled warning that the region’s digital backbone may now be in Iran’s line of fire.

events.title: Iran executes former atomic agency employee over alleged spying for Israel
events.summary: Iran executed a man early on Wednesday after convicting him of spying for Israel, with the judiciary identifying him as Mehdi Farid and saying he had worked at a “sensitive organization” and maintained online contact with Mossad officers.

events.title: Strikes on petrochemical hubs leave Iran short of plastics
events.summary: Iran is facing severe shortages of key petrochemical products after recent strikes on its main production hubs, according to two informed sources inside the country.

events.title: War or economic collapse: can Iran withstand the pressure?
events.summary: Iran’s economy is likely to buckle faster than the United States or the global economy under the combined pressure of war, sanctions, a US blockade and Tehran’s disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, experts said at Iran International’s townhall in Washington DC.

events.summary: Mounting opposition to negotiations with Washington in Tehran is casting doubt over whether Iran will proceed with a new round of talks with the United States in Islamabad as the ceasefire deadline approaches.

events.title: Tehran moderates see ‘no deal–no war’ limbo as worst outcome
events.summary: Tehran’s commentariat is warning that the most troubling outcome of the current negotiations with Washington may be neither war nor peace, but a prolonged “no deal–no war” limbo.

events.title: The future has been switched off here
events.summary: I am online again after 51 days. It is difficult to describe what things feel like here in Tehran. Bad is not quite the word. Weird, perhaps. Unreal.

events.title: Top condom maker plans price hikes of up to 30% amid US-Iran war impact
events.summary: Malaysia’s Karex Bhd, the world’s largest condom producer, plans to raise prices by 20% to 30% and possibly more if supply chain disruptions linked to the Iran war persist, its chief executive told Reuters.

events.title: Family told missing teen was alive, then received his body 60 days later
events.summary: A 14-year-old student disappeared during protests near Tehran on January 8, only for his family to receive his body 60 days later with a gunshot wound to the temple, Iran International has learned.

events.title: Lights out, then gunfire: Witnesses recount Mashhad protest crackdown
events.summary: A 32-year-old protester in Mashhad, northeastern Iran, stood in the street as the lights flickered out and the mobile network went dead, believing he had only a one-in-five chance of making it out alive.

events.title: Scam messages seek crypto for ships’ safe passage through Hormuz, firm warns
events.summary: Fraudulent messages offering ships safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for cryptocurrency have been sent to some shipping companies, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing a maritime security firm.

events.title: Iran executes man as January protest crackdown continues
events.summary: Iran executed a man on Tuesday over accusations that he set fire to a mosque and what authorities described as anti-security activities, according to the judiciary, in a case tied to anti-establishment protests earlier this year.

events.title: Is Iran entering its Gorbachev moment?
events.summary: The idea of an “Iranian Gorbachev” has surfaced before in the Islamic Republic, but this time the conditions may be different.

events.title: Iran crackdown reaches cemeteries as graves of slain protesters defaced
events.summary: Iranian authorities have stepped up pressure on families of those killed in January protests, defacing, destroying or covering graves with cement in the northern city of Rasht and the capital Tehran, local sources told Iran International.

events.title: Iran diplomacy wobbles as factions compete to avoid looking soft on US
events.summary: Apparent divisions over negotiations with the United States may have strengthened the most confrontational elements within Iran’s political landscape and facilitated the rise of new hardline actors.

events.title: The politics of pink: how Iran uses cuteness to rebrand violence
events.summary: Pink missiles, pink drones and pink firearms. Women with uncovered hair—braids, ponytails, short bobs—stood beside weapons, waved flags and smiled for cameras in scenes broadcast across Iranian media. Tehran appears willing to try almost anything to preserve power.

events.title: Bread shortages, soaring prices strain households in Iran, residents say
events.summary: Bread shortages and steep price hikes are undermining access to a key staple for many in Iran, with citizen accounts received by Iran International describing long lines, flour shortages and prices far exceeding official rates.

events.title: Iran says no decision yet on talks as Pakistan prepares to host US team
events.summary: Iran said on Monday it had not yet decided whether to join a second round of talks with the United States, even as Pakistan prepared to host a US delegation, with Tehran accusing Washington of violating the ceasefire and showing no real seriousness about diplomacy.

events.title: War-hit homeowners feel abandoned as Iran’s reconstruction aid fades
events.summary: The Iranian government has stepped back from earlier promises to compensate homeowners whose properties were destroyed in US-Israeli strikes, triggering anger among residents who expected the state to take responsibility for rebuilding.

events.title: 100 days on: the anatomy of Iran’s January crackdown
events.summary: One hundred days after protests erupted across Iran in January 2026, the events still stand out as one of the most widespread and violent protest waves the country has seen in recent years.

events.title: 100 days on: why Iran’s January protests spread across social classes
events.summary: One hundred days after protests erupted across Iran in January 2026, the events continue to reveal something fundamental about Iranian society: many people now fear silence more than they fear protest.

events.summary: To ask the Minister for the Cabinet Office, how many people aged 18 and over immigrated to the UK in each year from 2022 to 2025 from (a) Pakistan, (b) Kuwait, (c) Afghanistan, (d) Qatar, (e) the United Arab Emirates, (f) Sudan, (g) Mauritania, (h) Iraq,

events.title: Ghalibaf defends Iran-US talks amid hardline backlash
events.summary: Iran’s lead negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf defended indirect talks with the United States in a televised interview Saturday after hardline critics accused him of “betrayal” and even hinted at a “coup” over the negotiations in Islamabad.

events.title: From instability to influence: Pakistan’s pivotal role in US-Iran diplomacy
events.summary: Despite deep political turmoil, economic distress, militant violence, and a fraying security landscape at home, Pakistan has unexpectedly emerged as the publicly acknowledged central mediator between Washington and Tehran.

events.title: A nation in limbo: 100 days after the massacre, has the world moved on?
events.summary: One hundred days after one of the deadliest crackdowns in modern history, Iran remains suspended between grief and uncertainty, with a fractured public mood as some see justice in recent blows to the regime, while others feel left behind with it still in place.

events.title: 100 days after carnage: Iran economy reels from war, inflation, unemployment
events.summary: One hundred days after thousands of protesters were massacred on January 8 and 9, Iran's already fragile economy has sharply deteriorated, with millions feared to be unemployed as a devastating war compounds the crisis and accelerates economic collapse.

events.title: Iranian assaulted in London amid concern over threats to regime critics
events.summary: Iran International has received reports that an Iranian man was violently assaulted in central London. The Metropolitan Police are understood to be investigating.

events.title: IRGC fires at Indian vessel in Hormuz
events.summary: Two vessels, including an Indian-flagged supertanker, were forced back out of the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday after being approached by Iranian Revolutionary Guards’ naval units, shipping monitor TankerTrackers said.

events.title: The Hormuz get out of jail card turned to a grave
events.summary: For decades the IRGC relied on its ability to threaten closure of the Strait of Hormuz as its premier economic shield and golden get out of jail card.

events.title: Too early to tell who is winning Iran war, experts say
events.summary: As Washington signals that a deal with Tehran may be close, a central question remains unresolved: who, if anyone, is actually winning?

events.source: UK Government — Prime Minister's Office, 10 Downing Street
events.title: PM meeting with President Macron of France: 17 April 2026
events.summary: The Prime Minister met the President of France, Emmanuel Macron, in Paris this morning, ahead of talks with partners on the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: State media slam Araghchi's Hormuz tweet, say it let Trump claim victory
events.summary: Iran's state media issued rare and sharply worded criticism of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and the negotiating team after he declared the reopening of Hormuz Strait on X, saying the move created confusion and gave Trump an opening to claim victory.

events.title: Three charged over attempted arson at Iran International office in London
events.summary: British police on Friday have charged three people over an attempted arson attack near the London offices of Iran International.

events.source: UK Parliament — written question to Ministry of Defence
events.title: Tabled: USA: Military Bases
events.summary: To ask the Secretary of State for Defence, what steps he is taking to help ensure UK compliance with the laws of war in relation to US bombing missions on Iran from UK bases.
